          PROJECT NO. 58481

      RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT
LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION STANDARDS
          UNDER PURA §37.0561

       Rule Language Draft_CLEAN
  1   §25.194. Large Load Interconnection Standards.

 2   (a)   Purpose and Scope. This section sets forth the standards and criteria for an electric utility,

 3         a municipally owned utility, and electric cooperative to interconnect a large load customer

 4         to the ERCOT system. Nothing in this section limits the authority of a municipally owned

 5         utility or an electric cooperative to impose electric service requirements for large load

 6         customers on their systems in addition to the standards adopted under this section.

 7

 8   (b)   Applicability. This section applies to a large load customer has not energized as of the

 9         effective date of this section and that seeks:

10         (1)    a new interconnection at a single site that is equal to or exceeds 75 megawatts

11                (MW);

12         (2)    an expanded interconnection at a single site that equals or exceeds 75 MW for the

13                first time;

14         (3)    an expanded interconnection at a single site that exceeds 75 MW and is expanding

15                by 75 MW or more; or

16         (4)    to co-locate with a generation resource.

17

18   (c)   Definitions. The following words and terms, when used in this section, have the following

19         meanings unless the context indicates otherwise:

20         (1)    Affiliate -- means:

21                (A)     a person who directly or indirectly owns or holds at least 5.0% of the voting

22                        securities of a large load customer;




                                                                                                    Page 1
  1         (B)    a person in a chain of successive ownership of at least 5.0% of the voting

 2                securities of a large load customer;

 3         (C)    a corporation that has at least 5.0% of its voting securities owned or

 4                controlled, directly or indirectly by a large load customer;

 5         (D)    a corporation that has at least 5.0% of its voting securities owned or

 6                controlled, directly or indirectly, by:

 7                (i)     a person who directly or indirectly owns or controls at least 5.0% of

 8                        the voting securities of a large load customer; or

 9                (ii)    a person in a chain of successive ownership of at least 5.0% of the

10                        voting securities of a large load customer; or

11         (E)    a person who is an officer or director of a large load customer in a chain of

12                successive ownership of at least 5.0% of the voting securities of a large load

13                customer.

14   (2)   Backup generating facilities -- Generation facilities or energy storage facilities

15         that are not capable of operating, or are not configured to operate, in parallel with

16         the ERCOT system and cannot export energy to the ERCOT system.

17   (3)   Batch zero interconnection study -- The set of studies that are required by

18         ERCOT protocols before a large load customer meeting the requirements of

19         ERCOT Planning Guide Section 9, effective as of the effective date of this section,

20         can be interconnected.

21   (4)   Batch zero load -- A large load customer that meeting the requirements of ERCOT

22         Planning Guide Section 9, effective as of the effective date of this section, and is

23         included in ERCOT’s batch zero interconnection study.




                                                                                           Page 2
  1   (5)    Contracted peak demand -- The total non-coincident peak demand that a large

 2          load customer requests that an interconnecting DSP or an interconnecting TSP

 3          serve at a single site and is ultimately allocated by ERCOT, as stated in the SLLIA.

 4   (6)    Controllable load resource -- Controllable load resource as that term is defined in

 5          ERCOT protocols.

 6   (7)    Direct interconnection costs -- Direct interconnection costs, as that term is defined

 7          in §25.192 of this title (relating to Transmission Service Rates).

 8   (8)    End-use customer -- The entity that ultimately consumes power.

 9   (9)    Interconnecting distribution service provider (DSP) -- The electric utility,

10          municipally owned utility, or electric cooperative that is certificated or otherwise

11          authorized to provide either retail electric service or retail electric delivery service

12          at the location in which the large load customer’s consuming facility is located.

13   (10)   Interconnecting transmission service provider (TSP) -- The electric utility,

14          municipally owned utility, or electric cooperative that owns or operates the

15          equipment or facilities necessary to transmit or distribute electricity to the large

16          load customer.

17   (11)   Interconnection agreement -- An agreement that was executed, before June 1,

18          2025, by a large load customer and the interconnecting DSP after completion of an

19          interconnection study that was validated by ERCOT; and that, at a minimum, sets

20          forth the obligations of a large load customer to pay its direct interconnection costs.

21   (12)   Interconnection study -- The set of studies that are required by ERCOT protocols

22          before a large load customer may be interconnected.




                                                                                               Page 3
  1         (13)   Intermediate agreement -- An agreement that is executed by a large load

 2                customer, the interconnecting DSP, and, if different from the interconnecting DSP,

 3                the interconnecting TSP before a large load customer’s load is included in an

 4                interconnection study and that, at a minimum, satisfies subsection (d) of this

 5                section.

 6         (14)   Large load customer -- An entity requesting a new or expanded interconnection

 7                where the customer’s total expected non-coincident peak demand at a single site is

 8                equal to or exceeds 75 MW, whether at transmission voltage or distribution voltage.

 9         (15)   On-site backup generating facilities -- Generation that is not capable of exporting

10                energy to the ERCOT system and that, in the aggregate, can serve at least 50% of

11                on-site demand.

12         (16)   Requested peak demand -- The total non-coincident peak demand that a large load

13                customer requests, prior to executing an interconnection agreement, that an

14                interconnecting DSP or an interconnecting TSP serve at a single site.

15         (17)   Standard large load interconnection agreement (SLLIA) -- A commission-

16                approved pro forma agreement that is executed by a large load customer, the

17                interconnecting DSP, and, if different from the interconnecting DSP, the

18                interconnecting TSP and that, at a minimum, complies with this section.

19         (18)   System upgrades -- System upgrades as defined in §25.192 of this title (relating to

20                Transmission Service Rates).

21

22   (d)   Intermediate agreement. Before a large load customer’s interconnection request is

23         included in an interconnection study, the large load customer must execute an intermediate




                                                                                                Page 4
  1   agreement with the interconnecting DSP and, if different from the interconnecting DSP,

 2   the interconnecting TSP. If the interconnecting DSP and the interconnecting TSP are

 3   different entities, the intermediate agreement must specifically identify each entity’s

 4   responsibilities under this section, including which entity will accept the study fee and

 5   financial security from the large load customer. The intermediate agreement must meet

 6   the requirements of this subsection.

 7   (1)    Required disclosures.

 8          (A)     Demonstration of site control.

 9                  (i)    A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting DSP or

10                         the interconnecting TSP the type of property interest that the large

11                         load customer holds for the proposed site of the load location. The

12                         large load customer must be able to demonstrate control of the

13                         proposed site of the load location through provision of one of the

14                         following legally binding property interests linking the large load

15                         customer and the site of the proposed load location:

16                         (I)     a lease agreement, signed and executed by the large load

17                                 customer or an affiliate of the large load customer, for one

18                                 or more parcels of land sufficient to accommodate the

19                                 customer’s planned facilities at the proposed load location

20                                 for a duration of at least five years from the date the large

21                                 load customer is expected to reach the requested peak

22                                 demand;




                                                                                           Page 5
  1                (II)    a deed, transferring ownership to the large load customer or

 2                        an affiliate of the large load customer, for one or more

 3                        parcels of land sufficient to accommodate the customer’s

 4                        planned facilities at the proposed load location; or

 5                (III)   an agreement, signed and executed by the large load

 6                        customer or an affiliate of the large load customer, with an

 7                        option to purchase or lease one or more parcels of land

 8                        sufficient to accommodate the customer’s planned facilities

 9                        at the proposed location. An agreement with an option to

10                        lease land must obligate the large load customer to lease the

11                        land for a duration of at least five years from the date the

12                        large load customer is expected to reach the requested peak

13                        demand.

14         (ii)   If the property interest is held by an affiliate, the large load customer

15                must be able to demonstrate an existing legally binding connection

16                linking itself, the affiliate if applicable, and the site of the proposed

17                load location.

18   (B)   Substantially similar interconnection request. A large load customer

19         must disclose to the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP

20         whether the large load customer, an affiliate of the large load customer, or

21         the end-use customer the large load customer has contracted to host is

22         pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request for electric service

23         in Texas either directly or through a third-party developer, the approval of

  1   which would result in the customer materially changing, delaying, or

 2   withdrawing the interconnection request.      A material change or delay

 3   includes a delay of one or more years to the project’s projected date to

 4   realize its requested peak demand, a 20% or greater change in the requested

 5   peak demand, or a change in the location for the point of interconnection.

 7          interconnection request for electric service the approval of which

 8          would result in the customer materially changing, delaying, or

 9          withdrawing the interconnection request, whether directly or

10          indirectly through an affiliate, third-party developer, or end-use

11          customer that the large load customer has contracted to host, must

12          disclose the following information to the interconnecting DSP or the

13          interconnecting TSP:

14          (I)     the ERCOT-assigned serial number for the substantially

15                  similar interconnection request, as applicable;

16          (II)    the location, including the power region and, if in the

17                  ERCOT region, the load zone, of the substantially similar

18                  interconnection request;

19          (III)   the requested peak demand of the substantially similar

20                  interconnection request;

21          (IV)    the anticipated timing of energization of the substantially

22                  similar interconnection request; and




                                                                           Page 7
  1                 (V)    the interconnecting DSP and, if different from the

 2                        interconnecting DSP, the interconnecting TSP associated

 3                        with the substantially similar interconnection request.

 4         (ii)    A large load customer that discloses a substantially similar

 5                 interconnection request under this subsection may anonymize

 6                 competitively sensitive information in its disclosure to the

 7                 interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP.

 8         (iii)   An interconnecting DSP and an interconnecting TSP must not sell,

 9                 share, or disclose information submitted to the interconnecting DSP

10                 or the interconnecting TSP under this subsection other than a

11                 disclosure to the commission or ERCOT.

12   (C)   Site-related studies and engineering services. A large load customer

13         must disclose to the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP the

14         large load customer’s expected development schedule and progress on site-

15         related studies and engineering services required for project development

16         before energization (e.g., geotechnical survey, water, wastewater, or gas).

17         A large load customer must provide updates or progress reports to the

18         interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP when requested.

19   (D)   State and local regulatory milestones and approvals. A large load

20         customer must disclose to the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting

21         TSP the large load customer’s plans, identifying project milestones

22         including expected timing and current progress for obtaining non-

23         ministerial discretionary approvals from state and local regulatory




                                                                                    Page 8
  1         authorities required for development before energization. Such approvals

 2         must include, as applicable, permits for water, air, or backup generation;

 3         abatements for noise, light pollution, or traffic impacts; and agreements

 4         related to emergency response or site security. A large load customer must

 5         provide updates or progress reports to the interconnecting DSP or the

 6         interconnecting TSP when requested.

 7   (E)   Schedule for phased energization of requested peak demand. A large

 8         load customer must disclose to the interconnecting DSP or the

 9         interconnecting TSP the expected schedule, including the month and year,

10         for phased energization of the requested peak demand expressed in MW,

11         power factor (PF), and megavolt-ampere reactive (MVAr) units.

12   (F)   Water. A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting DSP or

13         the interconnecting TSP:

14         (i)     the anticipated volume of water needed by the large load customer

15                 or end-use customer the large load customer has contracted to host;

16         (ii)    the type of water source that will be used (e.g., potable, non-potable,

17                 groundwater);

18         (iii)   the entity that will supply water to the large load customer or end-

19                 use customer the large load customer has contracted to host (e.g.,

20                 municipally owned utility, investor owned utility, self-provided);

21         (iv)    the cooling technology that will be used; and

22         (v)     any other related information.

  1   (G)   Backup generating facilities and on-site backup generating facilities. A

 2         large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting DSP or the

 3         interconnecting TSP whether the customer has or plans to have backup

 4         generating facilities or on-site backup generating facilities. If the large load

 5         customer has or plans to have backup generating facilities or on-site backup

 6         generating facilities, the large load customer must also disclose the

 7         following information:

 8         (i)     the nameplate capacity of each of the backup generating facilities

10         (ii)    the fuel source and operational characteristics of each of the backup

11                 generating facilities and on-site backup generating facilities, as

12                 applicable, including run hour limitations and fuel storage

13                 limitations under the existing environmental permits; and

14         (iii)   how quickly each of the backup generating facilities and on-site

15                 backup generating facilities, as applicable, can reach their full

16                 capacity to serve the load.

17   (H)   Power supply. A large load customer must disclose to the interconnecting

18         DSP or the interconnecting TSP how the large load customer plans to

19         procure power and whether the large load customer has or plans to have on-

20         site generation that is capable of being synchronously interconnected to the

21         ERCOT system and will provide power to the large load customer.

  1         (I)    Controllable load resource. A large load customer must disclose to the
